page: Microsoft Azure F4-1amds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the Famdsv7 family, virtualized on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 1 dedicated vCPU powered by an AMD processor alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 32.0 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with a GPU count of zero. Local storage consists of an integrated 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration supports Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The server architecture represents a constrained-core deployment within an AMD-based platform, offering high memory density per compute core. While classified under compute-optimized families, the allocation of 32.0 GB of RAM to a single dedicated vCPU creates an extreme 1:32 core-to-memory ratio. This setup delivers significant cost efficiency for software environments licensed on a per-core basis, allowing organizations to minimize licensing overhead while preserving access to large memory allocations and high-speed NVMe local scratch storage. The primary tradeoff is limited aggregate compute throughput, as multithreaded workloads will be constrained by the single available vCPU.

Workload fit centers on database systems, in-memory caches, and enterprise data processing tasks where per-core software licensing fees dominate operating expenses. The combination of 32.0 GB of memory and 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes the instance appropriate for relational database engines, transactional caching layers, memory-heavy batch jobs, and development environments that require a substantial memory footprint without requiring parallel processing power.

The server includes 472 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage with Premium Storage compatibility, while containing no hardware GPUs and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The instance fits transactional databases, memory caching systems, ETL tasks, and single-threaded data workloads.
